newsitem.title: NORWAY: DnB's Vital announces cost-cutting plan.
newsitem.headline: DnB's Vital announces cost-cutting plan.

text.p: Norway's largest life insurer Vital Forsikring ASA said on Monday it planned to cut operating costs by 116 million crowns a year, to take full effect from 1999.
The company said that as part of these measures it would reduce the workforce by 20 percent over the next two years.
Vital, which was taken over by Norway's largest commercial bank Den norske Bank (DnB) in January 1996, said it also would sell its loan portfolio to DnB.
The insurer posted on Monday a profit before minority interests of 1.16 billion crowns for the full-year 1996, up seven percent from 1.08 billion crowns a year earlier.
The bottom line came in at 245 million crowns, down from 330 million crowns.

Vital said its administrative result fell to a loss of 290 million crowns, compared with a 190 million crown deficit in the 12-month 1995 period, due to a 100 million crown provision for restructuring and redundancies and a writedown for a contract for the delivery of technology services.
Vital said the workforce cuts would be made through early retirement and redundancy packages, as well as transfers on loan to DnB. It will close officies in 10 towns around Norway.

"All life insurance companies are troubled by an administrative deficit. The goal of these measures is to reduce the administrative deficit from the company from 1998/1999," Vital said in a statement.
